approach: Make `Athena::retry` accept a Closed(Stale) job. In `dispatch` (run/mod.rs) a new `stale_retry` step runs when no other seed applies. It reads the stale job's kept candidate and base from its records and merges the candidate onto the current tip once, before any producer call, with `land::merge_kept_candidate`. That function is backed by a new `Git::merge_tree_report` (`merge-tree --write-tree --name-only -z`), which keeps a conflicted tree and its unquoted paths. The step applies only when the stale job's `dispatch_branch` equals the checked-out branch and both commits still exist; the ancestry condition of the last plan is dropped (finding 6). Otherwise the retry is the ordinary producer retry from the base. Clean merge: reuse `resume_candidate` with no planner and no producer. It re-merges against the prediction commit, builds the candidate from the merged tree, recomputes the change list and fingerprint, then runs admission, `check_and_verify` (checks, replay, verifier) and the unchanged `plan()` landing. A merge that adds nothing to the tip closes the job failed with a reason and no producer run. Conflict: the conflicted tree is committed as a seed and a producer retry starts from it through the existing `TreeRetrySeed` / `BaseThenTree` path. A gate between `producer_loop` and `candidate_stage` closes the job failed, before any check or verifier, if any conflicted path is unchanged from the seed or still holds marker lines. `plan()` and its fingerprint-equality bail are untouched. Also in this revision: README.md line 76 is updated; drain.rs:1654 stays unchanged and gets a test; the clean-merge test now observes the Replay record and what the verifier saw. D157 reverses alternative (d) of D10 and records what a clean-merge verifier does not get and what a failed conflict retry costs.

decisions.choice: Decide clean-vs-conflict at dispatch time on `head`, before the dispatch commit, in `land::merge_kept_candidate(git, old_base, tip, old_candidate)`. `resume_candidate` redoes the merge against the prediction commit P to build the tree.
decisions.reason: The seed choice (resume vs seeded producer) fixes the brief that goes into the prediction commit, so it must come first. P differs from `head` only under records/, and an admitted candidate changes nothing there, so the second merge cannot newly conflict; if it does, the job closes failed with a reason and nothing lands unverified.

rejected.option: Decide inside `Athena::retry` at reading time
rejected.why: The tip can move between `retry` and `go`; `go` must decide on the tip it dispatches on. `retry` only needs to accept the job.

rejected.option: Re-apply the old candidate's diff onto the new base, as `resume_candidate` does today
rejected.why: That overwrites the other job's changes to the same files. Only a three-way merge keeps both.

decisions.choice: Add `Git::merge_tree_report(base, ours, theirs) -> MergeReport { tree, conflicts }` using `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only -z --merge-base=<base>`. Parse by splitting stdout on NUL: first field is the tree (trim any newline), the following non-empty fields are conflicted paths, the first empty field ends them. Exit 1 still returns the tree and paths; any other exit is an error. Leave `merge_tree` (athena-git lib.rs:663) unchanged.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3: without `-z` git C-quotes paths with spaces, quotes or non-ASCII characters, so the gate's `snapshot.dir().join(path)` and `show_file(seed, path)` would look up a different path and wrongly count a missing file as unchanged. `merge_tree` returns None on a conflict and drops the tree; the producer seed needs the tree and paths. The flags need git 2.38 or later; D19 pins 2.40 and the unit test uses the exact flags.

rejected.option: Parse newline output of `--name-only` without `-z`
rejected.why: Quoted paths for unusual file names break the gate (finding 3).

rejected.option: Seed from the old candidate commit as `tree_seed` does for a rejected job
rejected.why: `BaseThenTree` would restore that commit's whole tree and undo the other job's landing; `tree_seed` refuses exactly that case (mod.rs 477-480).

rejected.option: On a conflict, plain retry from the new base with no seed
rejected.why: The request says to run the producer from the kept candidate; dropping it repeats the whole producer run.

decisions.choice: Build the clean path's `ResumeMark` from the stale job's committed Candidate and Verification records (stage Checks, empty check_runs). `report_gaps` and `left_criteria` stay empty, and D157 says so with the reason below.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. `report_gaps` and `left_criteria` exist only in `ResumeMark` (state.rs:491-493) and `Built` (producer.rs:31-35), which feed verification.rs:100-123 as notes to the verifier. I found no committed record that holds them, so they cannot be rebuilt from records. They describe the original producer report, which the verifier already judged when the stale job passed verification; the merged candidate is checked and verified afresh against its criteria. `settle_resume_marks` removes a job's mark when it closes with any outcome but an environment failure, so a stale job has none and the committed records are the only durable source.

rejected.option: Keep the resume mark when a job goes stale, so the gaps survive
rejected.why: It changes close-time bookkeeping for every job, and the mark would describe the old tree.

rejected.option: Add a new record to carry the gaps
rejected.why: A schema change for a note the verifier already weighed; outside the listed files.

decisions.choice: Keep the conflict gate between `producer_loop` and `candidate_stage` (run/mod.rs ~1497) instead of folding unresolved paths into the producer's send-back. `RunContext` gains `seeded_conflicts: Vec<String>` (empty for every other job). `unresolved_conflicts(ctx, &snapshot)` flags a path whose bytes in `snapshot.dir()` equal `git.show_file(seed_commit, path)` (missing on both sides counts as unchanged) or that `land::has_conflict_markers` flags (a line starting `<<<<<<< ` or `>>>>>>> `). A flagged path calls `self.failure(ctx, reason)` naming the paths, with no checks and no verifier. D157 and the risks state that a failed conflict retry loses the kept candidate on a later `athena retry`, because the failed job matches neither `qualifies_for_tree_retry` (Rejected only) nor `resumable_job`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5. Folding the paths into the existing send-back (producer.rs:262-341) is the better design, but producer.rs is outside the listed files; it is raised as an open question. The gate fits where the seed commit and snapshot are both known, and candidate.rs (governed by D08) stays untouched. Markers in non-compiled files pass the checks, and modify/delete or rename conflicts leave no markers, so a per-path 'the producer touched this and removed the markers' rule is the sound one. `Snapshot::unchanged_since_seed` covers the whole tree and core never calls it.

rejected.option: Fold the unresolved paths into the producer's one send-back (producer.rs)
rejected.why: Better for the user but widens the change to an unlisted file; left as a user question.

rejected.option: Rely on the checks to reject marker-filled trees
rejected.why: They miss Markdown, TOML and data files, and modify/delete conflicts that leave no markers.

rejected.option: Edit candidate.rs 134-150
rejected.why: Governed by D08; would need a D156 reconciliation.

rejected.option: Let a producer keep a seeded version of a conflicted path unchanged
rejected.why: The rule cannot tell that from an unresolved conflict, so such a retry fails with a reason naming the path. The cost is a failed retry, not a wrong landing.

decisions.choice: `stale_retry` applies only when the stale job's `dispatch_branch` (records.rs:633; recorded at mod.rs:1031) is non-empty and equals `self.git.current_branch()`, and `rev_parse` finds both the candidate and base commits. The ancestry condition `is_ancestor(old_base, head)` is dropped. Otherwise it returns None and the retry is the ordinary producer retry from the base.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 6. `merge-tree --merge-base=<old_base>` applies the candidate's change from old_base onto any head, so ancestry is not needed for the merge to be correct; the later `plan()` still requires the new base to be an ancestor of the landing head, and the new job's base is the tip. Dropping it means a job made stale by a non-ancestor base (land.rs:97-100) also benefits. The branch condition stays: a job can be stale because another branch was checked out (close.rs 273-289, Plan::OtherBranch), and landing its candidate onto that branch with no producer run is a different act. A missing commit cannot be merged. D157 and the CHANGELOG name these two fallback cases (other branch checked out; kept candidate or base commit gone) instead of 'any other stale job'.

rejected.option: Keep the ancestry gate
rejected.why: No concrete reason: the merge is correct without it, and it sends one of the two stale causes back to a full producer run.

rejected.option: Merge onto whatever branch is checked out and document it
rejected.why: It lands a candidate on a branch it was never dispatched on, unverified in that context.

decisions.choice: When the merge of the kept candidate onto P gives P's own tree, `resume_candidate` closes the retry job failed, with no producer run, with the reason 'the kept candidate's content is already on the branch tip (job <stale>)'.
decisions.reason: A plain retry would repeat the whole producer run for work that already landed, the cost this change exists to avoid.

rejected.option: Return None from `stale_retry` and run a producer retry from the base
rejected.why: It repeats the producer run for work already on the tip.

decisions.choice: Reuse `TreeRetrySeed` and the producer brief's existing fields for the conflict retry: `unmet` and `findings` empty, one redacted `must_address` line naming the stale job and the conflicted paths. briefs.rs is not touched.
decisions.reason: Keeps the change inside the listed files; the must-address line states the real situation.

rejected.option: Add a stale-specific section to `retry_section` in athena-context
rejected.why: A prompt-text change outside the listed files; left as a user question.

decisions.choice: Leave `plan()` in land.rs and the Plan::Stale arms in close.rs unchanged. The retry is a new job with a fresh `Verified` (new base, candidate, fingerprint), so the existing equality bail (land.rs 136-142) enforces 'verified content equals landed content'.
decisions.reason: What makes a job stale is out of scope.

rejected.option: Re-land the old stale job in place from `retry_landing`
rejected.why: Its Verified fingerprint is for the old tree; landing the merged tree under it is exactly what the fingerprint rule refuses.

It is documentation of the retry command, so it belongs to the change. It is raised as a user question because the brief's list omits it.

rejected.why: The documented behaviour of the command would be incomplete.

rejected.option: Edit the display.rs hint to name `athena retry`
rejected.why: Widens scope beyond the listed files; the hint is still accurate.

decisions.choice: Leave the drain's own copy of the rule at drain.rs:1654-1657 (`retry: matches!(other, Some(Rejected | Failed | TimedOut))`) unchanged, and add a drain test that a stale job is not retried by the drain.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. That guard is what keeps a stale job from being retried automatically, which is out of scope. A stale outcome falls into the `other` arm with `retry: false`.

risks.risk: The merge at `head` is clean but the merge against the prediction commit P (head plus dispatch records) conflicts.
risks.mitigation: `resume_candidate` redoes the three-way merge against P. On a conflict it calls `self.failure(ctx, ...)` and returns, so the job closes failed and nothing lands. An admitted candidate changes nothing under records/, so P's records-only difference cannot conflict.

risks.risk: A clean merge whose result equals the tip (the other job landed the same change) gives an empty candidate.
risks.mitigation: `resume_candidate` compares the merged tree with `tree_of(P)` and closes the job failed with 'the kept candidate's content is already on the branch tip (job X)', with no producer run. The `..._already_on_the_tip_...` lifecycle test covers it.

risks.risk: The kept candidate or base commit was garbage collected, or the stale job's dispatch branch is not the checked-out branch.
risks.mitigation: `stale_retry` returns None when `rev_parse` cannot find either commit or the branch differs; the job then runs an ordinary retry from the base, which is no worse than today. The other-branch lifecycle test covers the branch case. There is no ancestry gate: the three-way merge uses the recorded base explicitly, and `plan()` still requires the new base to be an ancestor at landing.

risks.risk: A producer leaves a conflict unresolved: markers in a non-compiled file, or a modify/delete or rename conflict with no markers.
risks.mitigation: The gate before `candidate_stage` closes the job failed, naming the paths, if any conflicted path is unchanged from the seed or still holds marker lines. No check or verifier runs on it. The unresolved-conflict lifecycle test covers it.

risks.risk: The gate fails a retry where the producer correctly keeps a conflicted path as seeded (for example keeps the modified side of a modify/delete conflict).
risks.mitigation: A deliberate cost, not a wrong landing; the reason names the path and D157 records the rule.

risks.risk: A failed conflict retry loses both the kept candidate and the producer's work: the failed job has no Candidate record and a later `athena retry` on it starts from the base (it matches neither `qualifies_for_tree_retry` nor `resumable_job`).
risks.mitigation: Stated in D157. The better design, folding the paths into the producer's single send-back, needs producer.rs and is raised as an open question. The user can still run `athena retry` on the original stale job again, which merges the candidate afresh.

risks.risk: Parallel jobs in this repository usually both add a bullet at the top of CHANGELOG.md or docs/decisions.md (plan.rs:461 lists them as shared append-only files), so the usual stale retry will take the conflict path and a producer run, not the clean no-producer path.
risks.mitigation: Stated in D157 and this plan so users are not surprised. The conflict path still seeds the producer from the conflicted tree. A union merge for append-only files is a separate request.

risks.risk: The clean-merge verifier does not receive the original producer's `report_gaps` and `left_criteria`.
risks.mitigation: They are held only in the resume mark, which a closed job no longer has; the stale job's verification already passed with them, and the merged tree is checked and verified afresh. D157 states this.

risks.risk: Someone later adds Stale to the drain's retry set and the drain retries stale jobs automatically.

demonstrations.method: End-to-end test against the real `Athena::retry`. A job really goes stale (the `a_governed_change_on_the_branch_makes_the_job_stale` hook style, lifecycle.rs:2027-2069), then `retry` on it. Plus reading.rs unit tests for `earlier_attempt_with`. A second test, `a_stale_job_from_another_branch_is_retried_from_scratch`, has the hook check out a branch `other` that holds the records (the OtherBranch route, close.rs 273-289; lifecycle.rs:1995 shows the checkout); `retry` and `go` run there.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle retry_accepts_a_stale_job && cargo test -p athena-core --lib reading::tests::a_stale_job_can_be_tried_again && cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle a_stale_job_from_another_branch_is_retried_from_scratch
demonstrations.observes: `athena.retry(stale_job, &Lines::default())` returns Ok with a Proposal whose request is `try again on <stale job>`; the old error for Stale is gone. In reading.rs `earlier_attempt` on a Stale job returns Some and still refuses Landed and Abandoned with the 'only a rejected or failed job' prefix. In the other-branch test exactly one Producer entry is recorded, the Reader/Producer/Verifier order is that of an ordinary retry, and the merged candidate is not landed.
demonstrations.fails_without: `earlier_attempt_with` (reading.rs:1362-1374) bails 'job .. is stale; only a rejected or failed job can be tried again', so `retry` returns Err and the unwrap fails. Without the branch gate, the other-branch test sees zero Producer entries.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::retry` (reading.rs ~1103) and `earlier_attempt_with`. Fixture `Fixture::new()`, `Scenario::default().script()` and the `during_verification` hook exist (tests/common/mod.rs:428, lifecycle.rs:2027). The reading.rs helpers `records_with` / `job_with_checks` exist (~4636). New tests are added in steps 4 and 11; git is real and nothing under test is mocked.

demonstrations.method: End-to-end test. Job A (default scenario: its candidate changes README.md) goes stale because the hook commits a governed change to src/lib.rs plus an intervention record during A's verification. Then `retry`, then `go` on the retry job. Count the roles the fake driver was invoked as between the end of A and the end of the retry. Then load the retry job's records and the verifier input. A second test, `..._already_on_the_tip_...`, makes the hook also write A's exact README.md text so the merge is empty.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle a_stale_job_whose_candidate_merges_cleanly_lands_on_retry_with_no_producer_run && cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle a_stale_job_whose_candidate_is_already_on_the_tip_fails_without_a_producer_run
demonstrations.observes: Clean test: the retry job finishes Landed. `Scenario.invocations` gains no `Role::Producer` entry after the stale job's close and gains a `Role::Verifier` entry. The retry job's Verification record has non-empty `checks`. A Replay record exists for the retry job; its `candidate_commit` equals the retry Candidate's `candidate_commit` (the merged commit) and its `base_commit` equals that Candidate's `base_commit` (the prediction commit). `seen_by_verifier` contains both A's README.md greeting and the hand edit to src/lib.rs. The landed tree holds both changes and the tip is the landing commit. Already-on-tip test: the retry job ends Failed with a reason containing 'already on the branch tip', no Producer or Verifier entry follows, and the tip's non-records tree is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the clean-merge path the retry is an ordinary producer retry, a Producer entry is recorded and the zero-producer assertion fails; there is also no Replay record on a merged candidate and the verifier never sees both edits. Without the three-way merge the hand change is overwritten or the job does not land. Without the equal-tree rule the merge gives an empty candidate or a producer retry runs.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `Athena::retry` then `Athena::go` (`dispatch`, mod.rs:823, then `resume_candidate`, mod.rs:522; replay in `check_and_verify`/`replay_stage`, ~1774). The fake driver `Scenario::script()` with the `invocations: Arc<Mutex<Vec<Role>>>` log and `seen_by_verifier` exist (common/mod.rs:430-433, push at 570). The `during_verification` hook exists (common/mod.rs:428, 637). Records are read with `Records::load` (lifecycle.rs:3607). The `stale_retry` step and the merged branch of `resume_candidate` are added in steps 6-8; the double implements no merge.

demonstrations.method: End-to-end tests with a wrapper `Script` around `Scenario::script()` that, for the second Producer invocation only, reads `spec.workdir` and overrides `FakeTurn.edits`; the reads are collected in an `Arc<Mutex<..>>` and asserted after `go` returns. The original candidate edits README.md and src/lib.rs line 1; the hook lands a different edit of src/lib.rs line 1 (plus the intervention record), so the merge conflicts on src/lib.rs only.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle a_stale_job_whose_candidate_conflicts_goes_to_a_producer_retry_seeded_from_it && cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle a_conflict_retry_whose_producer_leaves_the_conflict_unresolved_fails_before_the_checks
demonstrations.observes: Seeded test: exactly one Producer entry for the retry job. At the start of that call src/lib.rs in the producer's `workdir` held `<<<<<<<` markers and README.md already held A's greeting. The producer's brief names src/lib.rs and the stale job. The wrapper's edit rewrites only src/lib.rs. A Verifier entry has a higher index than that Producer entry, and the job lands with the README.md change and the resolved src/lib.rs. Unresolved test: the second producer call makes no edit (and a variant leaves the markers in place); the job ends Failed with a reason naming src/lib.rs, no Verifier entry follows the Producer entry, no checks are recorded, and the tip's non-records tree is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: A plain retry from the new base lacks the markers and the README.md change in the producer's work tree, so the work-tree assertions and the landed-README assertion fail. A clean-only implementation never reaches a producer. Without the gate, the unresolved seed goes to admission, the checks and the verifier (candidate.rs 134-150), a Verifier entry is recorded and the job is not failed.

Unit tests in land.rs (`merge_kept_candidate`, `has_conflict_markers`) and athena-git (`merge_tree_report`, including a path with a space and a non-ASCII character) cover the pieces.

demonstrations.observes: A new D157 after D156 states that it reverses alternative (d) 'Automatic re-verification on the new base' of D10, with the reason that stale landings now recur with parallel jobs. It has Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance. It records the dispatch-branch and commit-exists conditions (no ancestry condition), the already-on-tip failure, the conflict gate and its cost, the report-gaps note for the clean-merge verifier, the shared-append-only-file conflict expectation, and that the fingerprint rule and the exclusion of automatic re-verification stay. Line 297 is still one line and ends with the 'Reversed by D157' note. No added line contains 'superseded by', 'supersedes' or 'amends' followed by a D-number. `cargo test -p athena-cli --test backtest` passes.

One bullet at the top of `[Unreleased]` / `### Added` says only what the diff does: `athena retry` accepts a stale job; with the dispatch branch checked out and the kept commits present it merges the candidate onto the tip; a clean merge re-runs checks, replay and verification and lands with a new fingerprint and no producer run; a merge that adds nothing fails the retry; a conflict starts a producer retry from the conflicted tree and fails before the checks if a conflicted path is unchanged or holds markers; a stale job from another checked-out branch, or with its kept commits gone, is retried from the base. It lists `Git::merge_tree_report`, names the root cause and cites D157.
